exams.syllabus: Trinity Brass syllabus. Lists read from the board's official repertoire pages.
comps: Marks

Face-to-face: 3 pieces x22 (66; each marked fluency & accuracy 7, technical facility 7, communication & interpretation 8) + technical work 14 + two supporting tests 20 (Gr6-8: sight reading 10 + aural/improvisation 10); total 100. Initial: a short technical exercise instead of scales. Pass 60-74, Merit 75-86, Distinction 87-100 (45-59 Below Pass 1). Technical work format F2F: lip flexibility exercise (memory) then scales & arpeggios (memory; examiner picks from items of sets A and B combined, tongued/slurred as requested, scale then arpeggio, f or p; Gr6-8 major = scale+arpeggio, minor = melodic, harmonic, arpeggio; pace quavers) or exercises (prepare 3, one per group; candidate picks first, examiner picks one more; music allowed) or Gr6-8 orchestral/brass band extracts (prepare all 3, play two). Digital technical pathway: 3 pieces x22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10); technical work is one unit, candidate chooses scales set A or B (memory) or two exercises (different groups) or two extracts; digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x25 (8/8/9 components) = 100. UCAS: Gr6 8/10/12, Gr7 12/14/16, Gr8 18/24/30 pts (pass/merit/dist). Scale pace figures are minimum tempi for even quavers. Lip flexibility exercise notation is in the syllabus/Trinity brass resources (not reproduced here).
Choosing pieces

Three pieces from the current repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/brass): two accompanied from group A and one unaccompanied from group B (digital Repertoire-only: four pieces, at least two A and one B). Initial-Gr3: one group A piece may be a duet (horn, trumpet, cornet, flugelhorn, euphonium, baritone, trombone only; play upper part, duet partner on a brass instrument, no piano). Own composition allowed instead of a listed piece (accompanied replaces A, unaccompanied replaces B; must be notated, on stave at Gr6-8; durations 0.5-1 min Initial rising to 3.5-5 min Gr8). Observe repeats of 4 bars or fewer; da capo/dal segno observed; cadenzas optional; memory optional with no extra marks; no metronome. Recorded accompaniment allowed up to Gr3 in F2F (live piano from Gr4) and at all digital grades; non-piano accompaniment needs prior approval. Gr4+ (and Gr6-8 tuning) candidate tunes own instrument. Bb trumpet: related instrument allowed for one piece from Gr3. Eb soprano cornet may choose pieces from tenor horn list (and vice versa Gr6-8); bass trombone may swap group B for trombone group B. Euphonium list usable for tuba. Treble/bass clef options for euphonium, baritone, trombone, tuba.
Before you enter
None: no theory or lower-grade prerequisite for any grade.
Digital exams

Digital graded exams (from Dec 2024) are filmed as one continuous take and offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces, technical work, overall performance; no sight reading/aural/improvisation/musical knowledge, replaced by overall performance marks) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces). Backing tracks allowed in digital exams at all grades; same repertoire and technical lists as face-to-face.
sections: Lip flexibility exercise (Gr6, memory; download from Trinity brass resources) then EITHER Set A (1 oct, pace 72-120): F major (f tongued), F# minor (p tongued), whole-tone on F# (tongued), dom 7th in B (f slurred), augmented arpeggio on F# (p tongued); OR Set B: F# major (p tongued), F minor (f slurred), chromatic on F# (f tongued), dom 7th in B (p tongued), dim 7th on F# (f slurred); major = scale+arpeggio, minor = melodic, harmonic, arpeggio; OR two brass band extracts (Our Heritage vol 6, CMT2006): Bliss Kenilworth; Goffin Rhapsody in Brass; McCabe Cloudcatcher Fells.
Sight reading: unseen extract, 30s prep, approx two grades lower than the exam. Parameters: thirteenth range, dotted quaver/semiquaver, accel allegro.

Two tests (10 marks each): sight reading (mandatory; thirteenth range, dotted quaver/semiquaver, accel allegro) plus either aural or improvisation (16 bars (F#/C minor)). Aural: 8-bar harmonised piece, major key: time signature, dynamics, articulation, two other characteristics; modulation in first four bars (subdominant, dominant, relative minor, or key names); with copy locate two melody changes (pitch/rhythm).

p0599.d: The famous gypsy-style showpiece: a mournful slow introduction then accelerating fast sections with flashy runs, harmonics and a sultry middle part. Instantly recognisable.

s0993.d: The Suzuki Bourrée: a lively Baroque dance in duple time with a buoyant, detached character; practises crisp articulation and light, even phrasing.

s0743.d: Elgar's 'Morning Song' arranged in a tenor-clef study book; the lilting melody lies higher on the cello, training tenor-clef reading and singing tone in thumb-free upper positions.
s0743.rw: Lovely melody plus useful clef practice

w00250.d: Folk-song style piece about a soldier. Practises storytelling phrasing and rhythm.

w01278.d: Jim Parker's 'Ground Force', likely a bold piece over a repeating bass; practises rhythmic drive, articulation and range. Details assumed.

w05296.d: Puccini's famous tenor aria from Turandot in arrangement: long sustained phrases and a noble, rising climax. Trains breath control and expressive line.

w05422.d: Haydn's Gypsy Rondo, finale of Piano Trio in G: a brisk Hungarian-style rondo in G with a catchy folk-like refrain and crisp, quick articulation.

w05984.d: Jazz arrangement of Manning Sherwin's wartime ballad, 1940; practises melodic phrasing, swing feel and tasteful embellishment.

w06431.d: Romantic song-like melody for E-flat soprano cornet, adapted from a film theme by Cosma. Practises sustained lyrical playing and expressive phrasing in a high register.

w06432.d: Slow movement of Haydn's Trumpet Concerto in E flat, with a gentle singing melody. Practises legato, breath control and elegant Classical style.

w06433.d: Arrangement of the famous fanfare theme from Janáček's Sinfonietta. Practises bold, rhythmic brass playing and secure high notes.

w06434.d: Fats Waller's swing standard arranged for brass solo. Practises relaxed swing feel, jazz articulation and light phrasing.

w06435.d: Choice of two pieces from Alpine Adventures, a set of contrasting mountain-themed solos. Practises rhythmic control, dynamics and range.

w06436.d: Melodic study from a supplementary studies book. Practises tone, intervals and flexibility on E-flat cornet.

w06437.d: Choice of two short studies from a graded study book, focusing on rhythm and articulation. Practises tonguing, flexibility and stamina.

w06438.d: Choice of three dance pieces by Vizzutti from a book of jazz and world dances. Practises style-specific rhythms, articulation and range.

w06439.d: Lyrical cornet solo with a flowing mountain-inspired melody. Practises sustained tone, phrase length and expressive playing.

w06440.d: Hoagy Carmichael's classic song arranged for brass. Practises smooth legato, controlled long phrases and expressive rubato.

w06441.d: Arrangement of Donizetti's oboe solo for E-flat cornet. Practises lyrical operatic phrasing, flexibility and neat ornamentation.

w06442.d: Elgar's gentle piece from Nursery Suite arranged for solo brass. Practises delicate, refined tone, quiet dynamics and sensitive phrasing.

w06443.d: Choice of two reflective, hymn-like solos by Graham. Practises sustained tone, smooth legato and heartfelt phrasing.

w06444.d: Arrangement of Kodály's Háry János Suite theme, with Hungarian colour. Practises rhythmic character, accurate tonguing and flexible phrasing.

w06445.d: Short, cool-toned solo from Alpine Adventures with icy colour and driving rhythm. Practises control, dynamic contrast and tonguing.

w06446.d: Spooky, atmospheric solo for E-flat cornet with strong rhythmic drive. Practises style contrast, articulation and range.

w06447.d: Study arranged from a Bach keyboard prelude. Practises smooth, even running lines, breath planning and clean fingers.

w06448.d: Klezmer-style study with sliding, ornamented melody and dance rhythms. Practises ornaments, rhythmic flexibility and tonal colour.

w06449.d: Advanced etude from Vizzutti's trumpet method, focusing on lyrical and technical skills. Practises flexibility, range and articulation.

w06450.d: First movement of Boyce's Symphony no. 4 arranged for E-flat horn or cornet. Practises light, rhythmic Baroque articulation and agile phrasing.

w06451.d: Choice of two bold solos by Graham, one stately and one brisk. Practises control, endurance and rhythmic energy.

w06452.d: Brilliant first movement of Hummel's Trumpet Concerto in E major. Practises virtuoso Classical technique, wide leaps and long-breathed phrases.

w06453.d: Theme and variations on a Welsh melody for cornet. Practises varied styles and techniques: lyrical, brisk and virtuosic.

w06454.d: The Queen of the Night's coloratura aria from The Magic Flute arranged for cornet. Practises extreme agility, staccato leaps and high range.

w06455.d: First movement of Neruda's Trumpet Concerto, with cadenza. Practises elegant Baroque-style phrasing, agility and high register.

w06456.d: Brass-band-style variations on a familiar Victorian ballad. Practises lyrical tone, ornamental decoration and technical variations.

w06457.d: Rossini's cavatine from The Barber of Seville arranged for brass. Practises florid vocal lines, agility and refined style.

w06458.d: Lively concert piece with fast, rhythmic gestures. Practises tonguing, agility and rhythmic drive in a modern idiom.

w06459.d: Study from Brandt's 34 orchestral-style studies for trumpet. Practises rhythmic accuracy, endurance and tonal control.

w06460.d: Two studies from a graded study book at advanced level. Practises tonguing, flexibility and range.

w06461.d: Study based on the Greek syrtos dance in a lilting rhythm. Practises asymmetric rhythms, articulation and ornamentation.

w06462.d: Choice of two studies from a brass book targeting rhythm and technical control. Practises syncopation, accents and articulation.

Vizzutti: American trumpeter and composer of virtuosic and jazz-influenced works.
Kodály, arr. Green: Hungarian composer and music educator; wrote Háry János; arranged by Green.
Endresen: Norwegian composer of supplementary studies for brass.
Carmichael, arr. Iveson: American songwriter of jazz standards such as 'Stardust'; arranged by Iveson.
Hummel: Austrian classical-romantic composer and pianist, a student of Mozart.
Elgar, arr. Wallace: English composer of the Enigma Variations and Pomp and Circumstance marches; arranged by Wallace.
Mozart, arr. Golland: Austrian Classical composer of symphonies, concertos and operas; arranged by Golland.
Sparke: English composer best known for brass and wind band music and educational pieces.
Lawrence: Composer of graded exercises and studies for brass.
Brandt: Russian trumpeter and composer of orchestral studies for trumpet.
Haydn: Classical master, 'father of the symphony and string quartet', long employed by the Esterházy family.
Boyce, arr. Bissill: English Baroque composer, known for symphonies and church music; arranged by Bissill.
Donizetti, arr. Wallace: Italian opera composer of Lucia di Lammermoor and L'elisir d'amore; arranged by Wallace.
McKenzie: Composer of world-music-style pieces for trumpet.
Rossini, arr. Green: Italian opera composer of The Barber of Seville; arranged by Green.
Janáček, arr. Green: Czech composer of Sinfonietta and opera Jenůfa; arranged by Green.
Rimmer: English brass band composer and cornet soloist.
Miller: Composer and arranger of beginner and intermediate brass pieces.
Walton: English composer of Façade, Belshazzar's Feast and concertos for violin, viola and cello.
Waller, arr. Ramskill: American jazz pianist and composer of 'Ain't Misbehavin'; arranged by Ramskill.
Neruda: Bohemian violinist and composer, wrote a well-known trumpet concerto.
Cosma, arr. Greenwood: Romanian-French composer of film scores; arranged by Greenwood.
Bach, J S, arr. Piper: German Baroque master of counterpoint, composer of cantatas, concertos and keyboard works; arranged by Piper.
